title: U.S. House · Georgia's 8th District
area: South-central Georgia, including Warner Robins, Tifton, Moultrie, and Valdosta.

context.text: Cook Political Report rates this race Solid Republican; Decision Desk, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball also rate it Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Austin Scott
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Republican primary unopposed on the ballot after Vinson Watkins withdrew

summary.text: Austin Scott has represented Georgia's 8th Congressional District since 2011. He previously served in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1997 to 2010 and owned an insurance brokerage firm for nearly 20 years before being elected to Congress.

background.text: Born in Augusta, Georgia, in 1969; earned a B.B.A. in risk management and insurance from the University of Georgia in 1993.
Owned an insurance brokerage firm for nearly 20 years before running for Congress.
Served in the Georgia House of Representatives from 1997 to 2010.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves as Vice Chair of the House Committee on Agriculture and Chair of its General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit Subcommittee; also sits on the House Rules Committee, House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, and House Armed Services Committee.

record.text: Serves as Vice Chair of the House Committee on Agriculture and Chair of its General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit Subcommittee in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Kelly Esti
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary, defeating Justin Lucas

summary.text: Kelly Esti is an entrepreneur, scholar, U.S. Navy veteran, and Delta Air Lines analyst running for Georgia's 8th Congressional District. He holds a Ph.D. in public policy, an MBA in finance, and a B.A. in management, and previously served on the Fulton County Zoning Board and as a Hapeville Board of Appeals member.

background.text: Holds a Ph.D. in Public Policy, an MBA with a focus in Finance, and a B.A. in Management; enlisted in the U.S. Navy after high school and served as a nuclear-trained sailor.
Has worked with JPMorganChase, E*Trade Financial, UPS, and currently works as an analyst with Delta Air Lines.

Has served on the Fulton County Zoning Board, as a board member for the Main Street Academy charter school, as a Hapeville Board of Appeals member, and as Legislative Chair for Georgia Equality; describes himself as one of the founders of the city of South Fulton, Georgia.

priorities.text: Says he will commit to regular town halls and to making his congressional office "a place where citizens can come learn and be empowered through knowledge."
Wants to ensure wealthy individuals and large multinational corporations "pay their fair share of taxes" to fund infrastructure, rural broadband, education, and lower healthcare costs.
Proposes a Georgia intercity rail system ("the Georgia Intrastate Transit") connecting the state's large cities to reduce road wear, congestion, and pollution.

positions.summary: Wants wealthy individuals and large multinational corporations to pay more in taxes to fund infrastructure, education, and healthcare investments.
Lists reducing healthcare costs for families and young adults as a priority.

summary.text: Roman Coley Davis is an independent candidate for Georgia's 8th Congressional District whose campaign centers on veterans' advocacy and child protection.

priorities.text: Lists veterans advocacy, protecting children, and "ousting corruption" as key campaign messages.

sources.title: Georgia's 8th Congressional District election, 2026 (Candidate Connection survey responses)

researchNotes: Basic-tier research from Ballotpedia. Roman Coley Davis has little public footprint beyond his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers; no campaign website was located.
